Elena — thanks for sending, and welcome. I pulled in legal and product to make sure we answer concretely. Short answers up front:

- Telemetry retention: Redwood treats operational telemetry that is tied to a customer’s use of the service as Service Provider telemetry (limited use). Our standard retention for telemetry metadata used for reliability/ops is 90 days; aggregated anonymized telemetry can be retained longer for product improvement but is explicitly excluded from PII/sale.

- Onshore fallback: we have two options we can offer in contract:
  1) Regional routing + standby pool (we can commit to an onshore standby pool in the US as an SLA-backed fallback for specified instances), or
  2) Documented failover with guaranteed onshore routing within X minutes and an onshore-only deployment for a subset of customer traffic.

I want to be precise in contract language — looping in Laura (Legal) and Ben (Product infra) to align on exact phrasing and the maximum retention window we can commit to in the DPA.

I’ve attached an internal draft response for legal to review and will follow up with a suggested clause later this week.

David / Ben — quick internal alignment. Notes from Legal & Product: 

- Telemetry: Legal prefers to avoid hard-coded retention windows in the DPA for operational telemetry (we usually classify it as "operational diagnostic data" and commit to a maximum of 90 days in our standard SP exhibit). For regulated customers we can add an Annex that sets a shorter retention (30 / 60 days) if required. Suggested contract sentence: 

  "Redwood will process operational diagnostic data as Service Provider telemetry and will not sell such telemetry. Unless otherwise agreed in an Annex, Redwood will retain operational diagnostic telemetry for a maximum of 90 days to support service reliability and security investigations; aggregated or anonymized telemetry used for product improvement shall be de-identified and retained per Redwood's product analytics policy."

- Onshore fallback: From Prod infra (Ben): we can offer two contracting options with clear SLOs: 
  Option A (Onshore Standby Pool): Redwood will maintain an onshore (US) standby capacity pool sized to handle a customer's peak baseline QPS for failover events; failover initiation and routing into the standby pool will be completed within 30 minutes of detection. 
  Option B (Documented Failover): Redwood will provide documented failover runbooks and guaranteed regional routing to onshore endpoints within 2 hours of failover initiation.

Ben — can you confirm the 30-minute and 2-hour figures or propose realistic windows? Also confirm any incremental pricing or reserved capacity requirements we need to surface to the customer.

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposed language and a short pricing note for the standby pool. High level: 

1) Telemetry clause (proposed):
"Redwood will process operational diagnostic data generated in connection with the Customer’s use of the Service as Service Provider telemetry (limited use) and will not sell such telemetry. Unless otherwise set forth in a mutually executed Annex, Redwood will retain operational diagnostic telemetry for a maximum of ninety (90) days for purposes of service reliability and security investigations. Aggregated or de-identified telemetry used for product improvement shall be processed in a manner that prevents re-identification and may be retained longer per Redwood’s product analytics policy."

2) Onshore fallback options (proposed):
Option A — Onshore Standby Pool (contracted add-on): Redwood will maintain an onshore (United States) standby capacity pool sized to the Customer’s contracted baseline capacity. In the event of a regional outage or capacity constraint, Redwood will route Customer traffic to the onshore standby capacity within thirty (30) minutes of failover initiation. Availability of standby pool is subject to a reserved capacity commitment or monthly standby fee.

Option B — Documented Failover (standard): Redwood will provide documented runbooks and will route Customer traffic to onshore endpoints within two (2) hours of failover initiation. This option does not require reserved capacity but is subject to operational availability.

Next steps: If Gridline is comfortable with the proposed phrasing I can ask Legal to put this into redline form against your PDF and return a consolidated DPA. If you prefer, we can schedule a short call with your GC to walk through the options.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward quickly.
